clue.text: Facetious rule — put ginger cakes on top of salad?

parts.note: parkin is a sticky ginger cake from northern England; plural gives parkins
taken as written
slaw, short for coleslaw, is a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: An odd kitchen instruction to pile gingerbread on a side salad.
explanation.walkthrough: PARKIN is a sticky oat-and-ginger cake from Yorkshire; 'put' and 'top of' are links, the picture being cakes stacked over coleslaw.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue-in-cheek principle that work expands to fill the time available is a jokey law of bureaucracy.

clue.text: Harsh priest introduced to trip up settlers

indicators.note: one piece is introduced into the other, so it sits inside it
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to trip is to slip
harsh means grim
a Catholic priest is addressed as Father

explanation.surface: A stern cleric causes some colonists to stumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SLIP into PILS, and 'introduced to' puts GRIMFATHER inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Puritan colonists who sailed on the Mayflower in 1620 were early settlers of New England.

clue.text: What recidivist will do with frankincense, for instance?

definitions.meaning: a repeat offender will sin again
frankincense is an aromatic tree gum, an example of this substance

explanation.definitionFit: A habitual offender sins again, and frankincense is a gum resin from Boswellia trees.

clue.text: Conservatives are justified

definitions.meaning: Conservatives sit on the political right, so are in that wing
justified means having right on one's side

explanation.definitionFit: Being correct in an argument is being in the right; conservatives belong politically on the right wing.

clue.text: Nurse goes to shed for farewell do

parts.note: SEN is State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade
to doff a garment is to shed or take it off

explanation.surface: A nurse heads to the garden shed for a leaving party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut but is a verb, taking off clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A party held to wish someone well as they leave is a send-off.

clue.text: A river once more going over falls

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces going over are turned upside down, read in reverse

parts.note: once more means again

explanation.surface: A river flows again over a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' reverses ARAGAIN as a whole, giving NIAGARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border, so the name stands for those falls.

clue.text: Secure part of 10

definitions.meaning: to secure a door is to fasten it with a key
10 across is a waterway, and a chamber with gates for raising boats is part of one

explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something is to lock it, and a lock is a gated section of a canal.

clue.text: Buffeted by the elements, snakes exhibited distress

parts.note: a path that snakes winds about
someone who wept exhibited distress

explanation.surface: Caught in a storm, the reptiles were upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snakes' looks like a plural noun but is a verb, meaning twists.
explanation.definitionFit: A place or person battered by strong gales is described as windswept.

clue.text: Finished article retail outlet distributed everywhere

parts.note: something finished is all over
the is the definite article
a shop is a retail outlet

explanation.surface: Goods from a completed store are spread far and wide.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for scattered in disorder all around the place is a colloquial British phrase.

clue.text: America invades devastated Italian part of Iberia

indicators.note: one piece invades another, getting inside it
something devastated is wrecked, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for America, the United States

explanation.surface: An American force invades a ruined Italian in Spain or Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastated' rearranges the Italian letters to LITANIA, and 'invades' marks the insertion. Lusitania was a Roman province, roughly Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusitania was the Roman province covering most of modern Portugal, on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: Duct made of tin and aluminium

parts.note: a tin is a can
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A pipe made from a mix of two metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a tubular passage in anatomy, a channel or duct, as in the ear canal.

clue.text: Wander through the mountains

definitions.meaning: to wander is to roam freely
a chain of mountains is a mountain chain or line of peaks

explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to range, and a line of mountain peaks forms a range.

clue.text: Stop a lapidary stashing his raw material

indicators.note: the words stashing it keep the answer tucked away inside them

explanation.surface: A gem cutter is told to stop hoarding his stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' refers to the lapidary, a cutter and polisher of gemstones, whose raw material includes this stone.
explanation.definitionFit: This iridescent gemstone is something a lapidary cuts and polishes, so it is his working material.

clue.text: Anita's transposed and updated Christiania

indicators.note: its letters are transposed, swapped into a new order

parts.note: Anita Loos was the American writer of Gentlemen Prefer Blondes, so Anita's surname is meant

explanation.surface: A woman's letters are rearranged to update an old city name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anita's' asks for Anita Loos's surname; 'transposed' reorders LOOS. Christiania was the city's name until 1925.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital was called Christiania until it was renamed in 1925, so this is its modern name.

clue.text: Something sweet could make a bee's lunch

indicators.note: the letters could make something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A treat that might serve as an insect's midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' reorders the letters of A BEES LUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chelsea bun is a sticky rolled currant bun, a sweet bakery item.

clue.text: Mother's pet dog

parts.note: ma is mother, so mother's gives ma's
a pet is a fit of sulking, a tiff

explanation.surface: Mum's beloved dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like the beloved animal, but means a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large powerful breed of guard dog.

clue.text: A certain air apparent in main dwelling

parts.note: the main is old poetic usage for the open sea
a shanty is a crude dwelling, a shack

explanation.surface: A particular atmosphere shows in the principal home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' means a tune, not atmosphere; 'apparent in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea shanty is a rhythmic work song sung by sailors, a particular kind of tune.

clue.text: Sportsman appearing as the tale unfolded

indicators.note: as a tale unfolds its parts come out in a different order

explanation.surface: A sports figure emerges as the story develops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfolded' reorders THE TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a sportsman, especially one competing in track and field events.

clue.text: An evil woman imprisoned and shamed

indicators.note: one word is imprisoned, held inside another

parts.note: evil means bad
she is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A wicked woman is jailed and disgraced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' marks the insertion; 'evil woman' looks like one unit but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abashed is to be embarrassed and ashamed, so it can stand for shamed.

clue.text: Citadel demolished, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: a fortress demolished has its parts broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A fortress is razed, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' reorders CITADEL; 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language, a local way of talking.

clue.text: Organisation gave leave to Italian songster

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, an organisation
to let is to give leave or permit
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A company granted time off to an Italian singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole tit is an older spelling of the small songbird more often spelt coal tit.
explanation.definitionFit: This small black-capped titmouse is a singing bird, so it is a songster.

clue.text: Strengthen new link between businesses

parts.note: Co, short for company, is a business
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: Bolster a fresh connection between companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'link between' places N between the two business words, though the clue mentions it before them.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm a belief or arrangement is to strengthen or reinforce it.

clue.text: Bound to laugh

definitions.meaning: a boundary, here a sunken ditch-fence bounding a park
the sound of laughter written out

explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch used as a boundary in English landscaped gardens, invisible from the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken fence marks the edge of grounds, and the doubled syllable is written laughter.

clue.text: This sounds like insufficient punishment for murderer

indicators.note: says the word that follows is said the same as the entry

parts.note: the cane, a beating with a rod, was a school punishment

explanation.surface: Caning seems far too mild a penalty for a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insufficient' belongs to the surface: a caning would be too little for killing a brother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Cain killed his brother Abel, the first murderer in the Bible.

clue.text: Bird dog's not black

indicators.note: not means the named letter is left out

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A dog that is not black turns out to be a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Some tack all the way round

definitions.meaning: tack is horse equipment, and this strap round a horse's belly holding the saddle is part of it

explanation.definitionFit: A saddle strap is part of a horse's harness, and circumference is the measure around the waist.

clue.text: Elegant young woman? Not entirely

indicators.note: the word is not given entirely, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: chick is slang for a young woman

explanation.surface: A stylish girl, or at least partly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' drops the last letter from CHICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and fashionable, a synonym for elegant.

clue.text: Agricultural business with secondary office lacking head

indicators.note: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a branch is a secondary office of a company

explanation.surface: A farming firm with a regional office that has no manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking head' looks like it means no boss, but it drops the first letter of BRANCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for raising livestock, an agricultural enterprise.

clue.text: Hot food given to pheasants around capital

indicators.note: the whole sequence is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
grub is slang for food
a nide is a brood or nest of pheasants

explanation.surface: Spicy fare is fed to game birds near a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses HGRUBNIDE. NIDE is an old collective noun for pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: Edinburgh is the capital city of Scotland.

clue.text: This many chaps revealed at sea

definitions.text: This many chaps revealed at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: This is how many men were exposed out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' reorders THIS MANY CHAPS; the whole clue also hints at seamanship, as an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill at sailing yachts is displayed by sailors on the water, matching chaps showing their prowess at sea.
